column3: NKJV has “went up together,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “Peter and John were going up.”
NKJV has “the lame man who was healed,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “as he held on.”
NKJV has “The God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text repeats “the God of” before each name.
Close to the Greek; “Author” is rendered “Prince.”
NKJV joins “so that times of refreshing may come …” to verse 19; the critical text places it in verse 20. “Turn again” is rendered “be converted.”
NKJV has “who was preached to you before,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “who was appointed for you.”
NKJV includes “all,” following the Textus Receptus. “From of old” is rendered “since the world began.”
NKJV includes “to the fathers,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text lacks it.
NKJV has “our fathers,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “your fathers.”
NKJV includes “Jesus,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “His Servant.”
